points.t: Scalp itch (or none), nape/behind-ear excoriation, and a live louse found on detection combing.
Pediculus humanus capitis crawls head-to-head; itch is hypersensitivity to saliva. Eggs are cemented to the hair shaft.
Treat only live infestation. Wet combing or dimeticone 4% (repeat after 7 days); check all household members the same day.
No live louse means no treatment. Pubic lice on a child’s eyelashes need a safeguarding pathway.

points: Spread is by **direct head-to-head contact**. Lice crawl; they cannot jump, fly or swim. Hats and brushes rarely matter because lice die within about 1–2 days off the scalp.
Females glue eggs near the scalp. Eggs hatch in about 7–10 days; adults live about 3–4 weeks on the host.
**Nits** are empty white egg cases that move out as hair grows. Nits far from the scalp usually mean an old infestation.
Itch may take **4–6 weeks** to appear at first infestation; many children never itch.
Scalp itch (often absent), tickling, and excoriations — especially **behind the ears and at the nape**.
Live grey-brown lice that move away from light; eggs/nits cemented to the shaft.
Complications: secondary impetigo, occipital lymphadenopathy, eczematisation, sleep disturbance and school stigma.

Check **all household members** and treat only those with live lice, **all on the same day**.
Nits stay put; dandruff and hair casts brush or slide off.

cards.name: Seborrhoeic dermatitis / dandruff
cards.clue: Greasy or flaky scale that brushes off; no lice

cards.name: Hair casts
cards.clue: Tubular casts that slide along the shaft

cards.name: Scalp psoriasis
cards.clue: Thick scale beyond the hairline; nail or body plaques

cards.name: Tinea capitis
cards.clue: Broken hairs, alopecia, black dots; mycology

cards.name: Impetigo of the nape
cards.clue: Honey crust — look for lice as the driver

items.t: Infant under 6 months (wet combing only; seek advice if this fails).
Extensive secondary infection or severe eczematous scalp.
Pubic lice on a child’s eyelashes → safeguarding pathway.

pearls.t: There is **no school exclusion** and no need to boil-wash bedding or fumigate. Inform school only as local practice.
Asthma/eczema: prefer wet combing or aqueous dimeticone; avoid alcohol-based lotions.
Itch can persist a few days after cure; leftover nits alone do not mean failure.
UK teaching point: course materials that recommend permethrin for head lice are **out of step with CKS**.
